content.value_statement: Go error paths often lose context, duplicate logs, or expose internals. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concrete rules for safer Go errors.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use errors.New, fmt.Errorf, custom error types, sentinel errors, and samber/oops.
Shows how to preserve chains with %w and break public boundaries with %v.
Guides matching wrapped errors with errors.Is, errors.As, and Go 1.26 errors.AsType.
Uses errors.Join for validation, cleanup, and independent failure collection.
Applies the single handling rule with slog and structured attributes.
Provides evaluation prompts for common production error-handling traps.
limitations: It is guidance for AI coding agents, not a compiler or static analyzer.
It assumes Go projects can use recent standard library features when available.
samber/oops and slog helper libraries remain optional external dependencies.
Large audits still need human review for domain-specific error semantics.

use_cases.title: Service Developer
use_cases.description: Add context-rich returned errors without duplicate logs or high-cardinality messages.

use_cases.title: Code Reviewer
use_cases.description: Review pull requests for swallowed errors, unsafe panic use, and incorrect wrapped-error inspection.

use_cases.title: Platform Maintainer
use_cases.description: Standardize structured error logs and public boundary behavior across Go services.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go function for unchecked errors, lowercase messages, and useful wrapping context. Suggest minimal fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: one function or small change.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Wrapped Error Matching
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this Go code to use errors.Is and errors.As correctly. Preserve behavior for wrapped errors and explain each change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: existing handlers with sentinels or custom errors.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize Production Logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Modernize this Go error path with slog and structured attributes. Follow the single handling rule and avoid high-cardinality messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: service code with logging and returned errors.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Error Strategy Across Modules
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Go packages for error creation, wrapping, panic recovery, joined errors, and public API boundaries. Return prioritized findings and fixes.

output_examples.input: A service function logs a database failure and then returns the same wrapped error.
output_examples.output: Flags the duplicate handling, recommends returning contextual error once, and moves logging to the boundary.

output_examples.input: A public gateway wraps backend errors with chain-preserving context.
output_examples.output: Explains that public boundaries should translate errors and avoid exposing backend types through unwrapping.

output_examples.input: A validator stops at the first invalid field.
output_examples.output: Recommends collecting independent validation failures and returning a joined error with stable messages.

best_practices: Use %w inside module boundaries and %v when intentionally hiding internal error types.
Log or return each error once, with structured attributes for IDs and counts.
Keep stable messages lowercase and low-cardinality; place variable data in attributes.
anti_patterns: Discarding returned errors with blank identifiers or using results before checking errors.
Logging an error at every layer and returning it again.
Interpolating user, tenant, path, or row IDs into stable production messages.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: It documents Go error handling. It may guide compatible agents that can run Go, git, or lint commands if the user asks.

faq.question: Can it fix code automatically?
faq.answer: In compatible coding agents, it can guide edits for Go error handling. Users should review generated changes before merging.

faq.question: Does it require samber/oops?
faq.answer: No. The skill explains standard library patterns first and presents samber/oops as an optional production error helper.

faq.question: What Go versions does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers errors.Join from Go 1.20, slog from Go 1.21, and mentions errors.AsType for Go 1.26+.

faq.question: How does it treat public API boundaries?
faq.answer: It recommends translating internal errors and using non-wrapping formatting when exposing chains would leak implementation details.

faq.question: Is it only for new code?
faq.answer: No. It supports new code, pull request review, and broader audits of existing Go services.
